summary: Cheboygan Crib Light, lit 1884 on an iron tower on a crib at the Cheboygan River mouth; no dedicated keeper; the crib was taken down and the tower moved ashore to Gordon Turner Park.

light.characteristic: fixed red until 1925; red flash every two seconds from 1925 (LighthouseFriends)

lens.note: Fourth-order Fresnel lens, made in Paris by Barbier, Benard & Turenne; originally used in the tower (LighthouseFriends).

structures.type: timber crib, about forty feet square, with stone fill
structures.note: Pier built 1881 in sixteen feet of water and repaired several times by 1902 (LighthouseFriends). Stone filling placed in 1899 (Board report). Demolition date not given in the sources read.
Thirty-three feet (LighthouseFriends). Now on a new cement foundation at the foot of the pier in Gordon Turner Park.

structures.type: two-room assistant keeper dwelling on the crib
structures.note: Quarters built in the year ended 30 June 1897 (Board report, scan p. 420); LighthouseFriends dates the two-room dwelling to 1897.

structures.type: brick and concrete pier replacing the wooden upper crib
structures.note: Oil cellar, dwelling cellar and foundation for the tower (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Grounds open at Gordon Turner Park; tower closed (LighthouseFriends).

visit.note: Boardwalk from Gordon Turner Park to the river and the light (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Iron pierhead beacon on an oak-ring crib at the end of the dredged channel; contract 15 October 1884 (Board report 1885, quoted by LighthouseFriends).
Iron boat davits placed on the crib (Board report, fiscal year ended 1892).
Quarters built for the assistant keeper on the crib, with pile protection for the boat (Board report, fiscal year ended 30 June 1897, scan p. 420). LighthouseFriends dates the dwelling to 1897.
Crib riprapped with stone, stone filling placed, timberwork leveled and deck relaid (Board report, fiscal year ended 1899).
Wooden upper crib cut down; brick and concrete pier built (LighthouseFriends).
1,200-pound fog bell hung from a skeleton tower on the crib (LighthouseFriends).
Changed to a red flash every two seconds on 12 June 1925 (LighthouseFriends). Bulletin index lists a change in illuminant for the crib in the 1924-1929 volumes, not read.
Gas-operated fog-bell striker installed on 12 June 1925 (LighthouseFriends quoting the Bulletin).
Windows replaced, joints recaulked and repainted by Great Lakes Lighthouse Keepers Association volunteers (LighthouseFriends).
Coast Guard lists the structure as nonessential property; transfer to the City of Cheboygan begun (LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1884 date for the beacon is confirmed by the 1885 Board report as quoted by LighthouseFriends (contract 15 October 1884, lighted 1 November 1884). The quarters entry sits in the Board report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1897 (scan p. 420), not 1896; it agrees with LighthouseFriends' 1897.
The Board report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1897 records the quarters; LighthouseFriends dates the two-room dwelling to 1897. No disagreement once the report year is corrected.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard had the crib removed and the iron tower was set on a new foundation at the foot of the pier in Gordon Turner Park.
LighthouseFriends gives the tower as thirty-three feet (about 10 m). The record's 7.5 m (about 25 ft) is not sourced in the material read.

notes_for_editor:
No keepers are named in any source read; the archive roster for the station is empty. LighthouseFriends says an assistant keeper of the Cheboygan River Range Lights looked after the crib; those keepers are not named here.
Conflicts left open: (1) quarters: resolved. The entry at scan 420 is in the Board report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1897, not 1896 (the 1896 volume's grep label covers both reports; the text puts this entry after the 1897 report header); LighthouseFriends' 1897 agrees. (2) tower height: LighthouseFriends 33 ft (about 10 m); the record 7.5 m (25 ft). (3) focal height in the record (7.6 m) not checked against any source read. (4) 1925 change: LighthouseFriends says the characteristic changed to a red flash every two seconds; the Board's 1924-29 index (not read) has an entry "Cheboygan Crib, change in illuminant", which may be the same change.
Automation date: LighthouseFriends says "late 1920s"; Wikipedia gives 1920 (lead only, not cited).
Deactivation 1984 (record, from Rowlett) is not verified by any source read.
The 1885 Board report quotation comes from LighthouseFriends; the 1885 volume is not in the local corpus.
Crib demolition date is not given in the sources read. The tower's move to Gordon Turner Park is not dated.
Crib build date: LighthouseFriends says the pier was built in 1881 in sixteen feet of water (the record's 1884 is the beacon's date, not the crib's). Coordinates: the record's position (45.656, -84.465) is the crib's site, which LighthouseFriends also gives. The surviving tower stands on shore at the foot of the pier, so the record's point is probably wrong for the tower; no corrected coordinate is proposed.
Bulletin 1932 OCR is jumbled around the striker article; only its heading is quoted. The "installed on June 12, 1925" statement is LighthouseFriends' quotation and is attributed to it.
Storms, wrecks and rescues: none sourced for the crib in the material read; no chapter written.
Printed pages not read: Internet Archive citations use scan pages (1892 scan 542; 1897 scan 420; 1899 scan 220). Check the page images before printing a page number.
No photos mirrored: LighthouseFriends photographs are copyrighted. The Wikimedia Commons photo in the record is not checked for licence.
Verification 2026-10-27: story restructured with a 'The place' chapter; 'serious lean' changed to the source's 'significant lean'; crib foundation and grant wording rewritten. Board report pages checked in the corpus text: scan 542 (FY1892), 420 (FY1897, not FY1896), 220 (FY1899), Bulletin 1932 PDF p. 11 heading present in OCR.
